analysis.summary: HMH (a global oil & gas / marine technology company) is hiring a System Developer via NES Advantage Solutions on a 6-month contract (extendable) based in Kristiansand, in-office. The role is full-stack leaning backend — building cloud services, APIs, and integration layers for a long-running product. The team follows structured DevOps/CI/CD practices. HMH operates across 16 countries with a global engineering culture. NES is a global staffing firm with 80+ offices that explicitly handles visa and work permit logistics for contractors.
analysis.why_foreigner_friendly: Excellent fit for an English speaker. The job ad itself is written entirely in English, the working language is listed as both Norwegian and English, and English fluency is listed as a hard requirement while Norwegian is explicitly 'a plus' only. NES Advantage's own company blurb specifically states they help contractors secure visas and work permits — this is not boilerplate, it is their core value proposition. HMH is a global company with offices on five continents, so the team is accustomed to international colleagues. The main practical friction is Kristiansand (smaller city, requires relocation) and the in-office requirement. But for a foreigner needing visa support, a staffing agency that actively manages permit logistics is a significant structural advantage over applying directly.
